395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=

9	/-!
10	# Swallow or miss: the shape of an adaptation that can be certified
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows that the assembler's per-piece no-leak clause
13	*forces* the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed.  This file gives the matching
14	sufficient condition, and it is deliberately crude:
15	
16	> if every piece either **swallows** the support (`supportLocus ⊆ pieces j`) or **misses**
17	> it (`Disjoint supportLocus (pieces j)`), then no-leak holds at every piece.
18	
19	For a swallowing piece the trace is the whole support, which is closed by construction
20	(`isClosed_supportLocus`); for a missing piece the trace is empty.  Neither case needs a
21	fibre, a tube, or an idempotent.
22	
23	The crudeness is not a defect, because the necessity lemma pins down exactly how much
24	freedom is left.  Both pinned charts are covered by their pieces, so
25	
26	* if some chart-`b` piece meets the support it must swallow it, whence `supportLocus ⊆ V_b`;
27	* otherwise every chart-`b` piece misses the support, whence `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ∅`.
28	
29	Since `V₀ ⊔ V₁` is the whole relative curve, a nonempty support therefore lies in
30	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the divisor must avoid **both** vertical fibres `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — or be
31	confined to one of them.  That is the honest chart-design hypothesis of the lane, and it is
32	where the DD-R atlas has to do its work; it is not something a support tube, a packet
33	idempotent, or a shrink of the base can manufacture.
34	
35	A missing piece contributes nothing at all: its equation is a unit, so its colength module
36	vanishes (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`) and clauses (c1) hold there for
37	free — no fibrewise regularity input.  So the certificate of a swallow-or-miss adaptation is
38	carried entirely by the swallowing pieces, at most one per chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a
43	  piece missing the support has a vanishing colength.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — swallow
45	  or miss gives no-leak at that piece.

48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` —

51	  `…_chart₁_…` — the design constraint the shape imposes on the divisor.
52	-/

69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
71	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
72	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
73	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
74	
75	/-! ## A piece missing the support contributes nothing -/
76	
77	/-- **A piece that misses the support has a vanishing colength.** Its equation has a unit
78	germ at every point of the piece (`isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` read through the unit locus), hence
79	is a unit (`RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), hence spans the unit ideal.
80	
81	This is the colength companion of `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`: on
82	such a piece the certificate's clauses (c1) are free, with no fibrewise regularity input. -/
83	lemma subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (j : A.index)
84	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
85	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) := by
86	  have hunit : IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
87	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
88	    intro z hz
89	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
90	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hz).mpr
91	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
92	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr
93	    (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span rfl) hunit)
94	
95	/-! ## Swallow or miss gives no-leak -/
96	
97	/-- **Swallow or miss gives no-leak at that piece.** If the piece contains the whole support
98	its trace is the support, closed by `isClosed_supportLocus`; if the piece misses the support
99	its trace is empty.  In neither case is a fibre, a tube or an idempotent involved. -/
100	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint (j : A.index)
101	    (h : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
102	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
103	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
104	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
105	  rcases h with hsub | hdisj
106	  · rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
107	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus
108	  · rw [Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hdisj]
109	    exact isClosed_empty
110	
111	/-- **The assembler-shaped `hnoLeak` from swallow-or-miss.** This is the hypothesis of
112	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` /
113	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` /
114	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`, produced with no fibre analysis. -/
115	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
116	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
117	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
118	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
119	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
120	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
121	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
122	  intro j s x hx
123	  have hleak := A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j)
124	  by_contra hxU
125	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hleak x ⟨hx.2, hxU⟩
126	
127	section Finite
128	
129	/- The finiteness engine consumes the properness licence on the relative curve
130	(`instIsProperRelCurveHom`), so this clause — and only this clause — needs `IsProper`. -/
131	variable [IsProper C.hom]
132	
133	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite at every piece, from swallow-or-miss.** -/
134	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
135	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
136	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
137	    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := fun j =>
138	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
139	    (A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j))
140	
141	end Finite
142	
143	/-! ## What the shape forces on the divisor
144	
145	The necessity direction of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` is sharpened here: because the
146	chart-`b` pieces cover `V_b`, a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor that is
147	either inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it.  Combined with `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` this says a
148	nonempty support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, or is confined to one vertical fibre of `pi`.
149	
150	This is the statement the DD-R atlas owes: **the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and
151	`pi⁻¹(∞)`.**  It is a hypothesis about the chart, and it is the only remaining geometric
152	input of the (c1) side of the certificate. -/
153	
154	/-- **Chart-0 dichotomy.** A swallow-or-miss adaptation forces the support either inside the
155	pinned chart `V₀` or disjoint from it. -/
156	theorem subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀
157	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
158	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
161	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
162	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R))
163	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
164	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx)
165	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
166	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
167	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
168	    exact (h (Sum.inl j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
169	
170	/-- **Chart-1 dichotomy.** -/
171	theorem subset_chart₁_or_disjoint_chart₁
172	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
173	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
174	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
175	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
176	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
177	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R))
178	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
179	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx)
180	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
181	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
182	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
183	    exact (h (Sum.inr j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
184	
185	end DivisorAdaptation
186	
187	end AlgebraicGeometry
188

420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442	
443	end DivisorAdaptation
444	
445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)
448	
449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
459	
460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
468	
469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)
473	
474	namespace DivFam
475	
476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
477	
478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
485	
486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
490	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
491	
492	@[simp]
493	lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
494	    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
495	  rfl
496	
497	end DivFam
498	
499	end AlgebraicGeometry

====================================================================================================
ID: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate
TITLE: DD-R certificate: inherited certificate, epsilon projection, U1/U2, and inverse laws
STATUS: active PRIO: normal DEPS: [] INBOX: [] PINS: ['c843eafd7', '359c0a38d', '2ff846d74', '5e6d8ac6c']
SUMMARY:
ROUTE RE-BASED (2026-07-25, run 0048) — the lane's gate is now a single geometric statement
about the divisor, and it is PROVED to be irreducible.

THE NECESSITY (landed, kernel-checked, commit 49866bdd1, Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean).
A FinCoverData carries a partition of unity on each pinned chart, so the chart-b pieces cover
ALL of V_b and the union of their traces is the whole chart trace supportLocus cap V_b. A finite
union of closed sets is closed, hence

  the assembler's hnoLeak at every piece  ==>  supportLocus cap V_0 and supportLocus cap V_1 are
  CLOSED in the relative curve

(isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak). That mentions neither the adaptation nor its
pieces. Contrapositive not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart0: a system whose chart trace is not
closed admits NO adaptation satisfying the assembler's hypothesis. So refining the cover can only
add constraints, and shrinking the base only re-states the same condition over the smaller base.

THE SUFFICIENCY (landed, commit 206967379, Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean). If every piece
either SWALLOWS the support (supportLocus subset pieces j) or MISSES it, then no-leak holds at every
piece and clause (c1)-finite follows, with no fibre, no tube and no packet idempotent. A missing
piece has a UNIT equation, so its colength module VANISHES
(subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus) and needs no fibrewise regularity input either.
The two dichotomy theorems pin the shape: a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor
inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it, so (V_0 sup V_1 = top) a nonempty support lies in
V_0 cap V_1 — the divisor avoids BOTH vertical fibres of pi — or is confined to one of them.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OLD LEAVES. tube-fibre and leak-image are both superseded: their common
obligation is exactly chart-trace closedness, which is a CHART-DESIGN input, not something the
support tube / idempotent packets / base shrinking can manufacture. away-kerspan (hinj) is
suspected to be an ARTIFACT of certifying the arbitrary `.some` extraction adaptation: for a
swallow-or-miss adaptation the Cech complex has at most one nontrivial piece per chart and its
difference map is surjective onto the off-diagonal overlaps, so (c3)/(c4) should be free — see the
new cert-collapse leaf. That is the single highest-value experiment in the lane.

THE NEW CHAIN: chart-avoid -> swallow-adapt -> cert-collapse -> cert-assemble.

and its two named inputs are both retired: tube-fibre is superseded by chart-avoid, and away-kerspan
is suspected to be an artifact (see cert-collapse). The genuine remaining composition, together with

TITLE: Away-kerspan / hinj = certificate clause (c4): blocked, and likely an artifact of the .some adaptation
STATUS: blocked PRIO: low DEPS: [] INBOX: [] PINS: []
SUMMARY:
BLOCKED / LIKELY AN ARTIFACT — do not grind it before cert-collapse is tried (2026-07-25, run 0048).

STATUS OF THE MATHEMATICS. hinj (residue-fibre injectivity of the injectivized Cech difference,
Picard/DivSchemeCertZarKerSpan.lean:63,123) is not a decomposition of the certificate: it is
PROVABLY EQUIVALENT to clause (c4) itself, Module.Flat R (ovlProd / range (deltaLeft - deltaRight)),
via ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective (DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:56) plus
SlicingFlatKernel.lean. Two landed no-gos fence it: a cleverer submodule L cannot help (the L-free
form is already the general one), and support-separated pieces cannot help
(DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean:201/:257). Over a field it is free (every module is projective,
DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean); over a nonreduced base the escape is unavailable.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY AN ARTIFACT. Every attempt so far certified
ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation = (exists_divisorAdaptation ...).some

ID: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.cert-collapse
TITLE: Cert-collapse: (c2)/(c3)/(c4) — and the hinj wall — are free for a swallow-or-miss adaptation
STATUS: pending PRIO: urgent DEPS: [] INBOX: [] PINS: []
SUMMARY:
THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE EXPERIMENT IN THE LANE: show that clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) — and therefore
the hinj wall of away-kerspan — are FREE for a swallow-or-miss adaptation.

WHY THIS SHOULD WORK. The lane has been certifying `(exists_divisorAdaptation ...).some`
(ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation, Picard/DivSchemeFamily.lean:367) — an adaptation about which
NOTHING is known, so every clause had to be proved for an arbitrary finite cover. The pointwise gate
accepts ANY adaptation over the shrunken base, so choose one. For the swallow-or-miss shape:

 * every MISSING piece has a subsingleton colength AND subsingleton overlap colengths
   (subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus,
   subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus), so it contributes 0 to chartProd and to
   ovlProd;
 * only the two SWALLOWING pieces survive, one per chart, and every overlap colength among them is
   Gamma of the SAME divisor subscheme (the support is inside every one of those opens);
 * hence delta_left - delta_right is, up to the identifications, (a, b) |-> a - b, which is
   SURJECTIVE onto the off-diagonal overlap components. Its kernel W(d) is the diagonal, so
   W(d) iso colength, and coker(delta) is the diagonal part prod_j ovlColength j j iso prod_j
   colength j plus one leftover copy — all finite projective by (c1), hence FLAT.

So (c2) reduces to (c1) plus the rank, (c3)/(c4) are flatness of finite projective modules, and
hinj — provably equivalent to (c4) — is discharged by construction rather than by a fibrewise
flatness argument over a nonreduced base. If this lands, away-kerspan is retired, not solved.

THE ONE TECHNICAL LEMMA NEEDED: colength is invariant under shrinking a piece to a smaller open
that still contains the trace. Ring-level core: if V(g) cap V(h) = empty in a commutative ring then
h is a UNIT mod (g) (from 1 in span{g, h}), so Gamma(V)/(g) iso Gamma(V)_h/(g) = Gamma(D(h))/(g)
via IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen. Applied with g the piece equation and h cutting out the
smaller open, this identifies all the colength and overlap-colength modules of the swallowing
pieces. Watch the Opens-level `inf` bookkeeping (pieces i inf pieces j is not syntactically
symmetric).

its fibre at t = 0 is {0, infinity}. Hence the DD-R atlas must arrange the avoidance, e.g. by
choosing the pinned charts (the two P^1 fibres) per chart of DivScheme, or by carving the locus
where the divisor misses them. Both are open conditions.

already implies it — Pic0ChartLocusOpen / Pic0ChartLocusFibreField / DivSchemeEpsCarve are the
candidates; the theta window K subset H^0(Theta^a) makes the pole side (pi^{-1}(infinity))
tractable, since a generator with exact pole order a has no zero there.

TITLE: Swallow-adapt: build the 2-piece-per-chart adaptation (swallowing piece + comaximal complement)
STATUS: pending PRIO: high DEPS: [] INBOX: [] PINS: []
SUMMARY:
CONSTRUCT the swallow-or-miss adaptation, i.e. produce the input of
DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean).
Replaces away-assemble's "compose tube-fibre" framing.

SHAPE (2 pieces per chart, m_0 = m_1 = 2):
 (1) the SWALLOWING piece D(h_b) of chart b, with supportLocus subset D(h_b) and a single equation
     f_b in Gamma(D(h_b)) cutting d there;
 (2) the COMPLEMENTARY piece D(s_b) with Disjoint supportLocus D(s_b) and equation 1 — its eqn_rel
     clause is free because d's equation is a unit off the support, and its colength VANISHES.

THE TWO HONEST INPUTS:
 (a) chart-avoid, which gives supportLocus subset V_b so that a swallowing piece can exist at all;
 (b) A GLOBAL GENERATOR NEAR THE SUPPORT: some psi in K whose divisor agrees with d on a
     neighbourhood of supportLocus. A theta section has exactly two chart components
     (relThetaResSide a b), so psi supplies f_0 and f_1 simultaneously. div(psi) = d + E with E
     disjoint from the support, so W := relCurve \ supp(E) is an open containing supportLocus on
     which psi cuts d.

THE COMAXIMALITY STEP (elementary, no new geometry): supportLocus and V_b \ W are disjoint closed
subsets of the AFFINE V_b, so their ideals in Gamma(V_b) are comaximal: sigma + tau = 1 with sigma
vanishing on the support and tau on V_b \ W. Then h_b := tau gives supportLocus subset D(h_b)
subset W, s_b := sigma gives Disjoint supportLocus D(s_b), and span{h_b, s_b} = top is the required
partition of unity. Base shrinking is licensed throughout by the pointwise gate
isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation.

Spreading-out remark for (b): a line bundle trivial on the (finite over the base, hence semilocal
after localizing) divisor scheme is trivial after a Zariski shrink of the base, which is exactly the
freedom the pointwise gate provides.

142	def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] A') : DivFamZar C A π n ≃ DivFamZar C A' π n where
143	  toFun := mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom
144	  invFun := mapAlgHom e.symm.toAlgHom
145	  left_inv F := by
146	    rw [← mapAlgHom_comp, show e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k A from
147	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a, mapAlgHom_id]
148	  right_inv F := by
149	    rw [← mapAlgHom_comp, show e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k A' from
150	      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.apply_symm_apply a, mapAlgHom_id]
151	
152	/-- The transport along an isomorphism is `mapAlgHom` of its underlying map. -/
153	@[simp]
154	lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] A') (F : DivFamZar C A π n) :
155	    congr e F = mapAlgHom e.toAlgHom F :=
156	  rfl
157	
158	/-- The inverse transport along an isomorphism is `mapAlgHom` of the inverse map. -/
159	@[simp]
160	lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] A') (F : DivFamZar C A' π n) :
161	    (congr e).symm F = mapAlgHom e.symm.toAlgHom F :=
162	  rfl
163	
164	end DivFamZar
165	
166	/-- **`toZar` intertwines the explicit-face base changes**: the comparison from
167	globally certified to locally certified classes is natural in the test algebra along an
168	explicit `k`-algebra map — `DivFam.toZar_mapAlg` at the induced tower. -/
169	lemma DivFam.toZar_mapAlgHom {A A' : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing A']
170	    [Algebra k A'] (φ : A →ₐ[k] A') (F : DivFam C A π n) :
171	    (DivFam.mapAlgHom φ F).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom φ F.toZar :=
172	  letI : Algebra A A' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
173	  haveI : IsScalarTower k A A' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
174	  DivFam.toZar_mapAlg A' n F
175	
176	/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/
177	
178	variable (C π n)
179	
180	/-- **The locally certified divisor functor at an arbitrary test object**
181	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6 on the Addendum-2 carrier; the `divFam` vehicle):
182	compatible families of locally certified divisor classes over the affine opens of
183	`T.left` — the value at a smaller affine open is the base change of the value at a
184	larger one along the section-restriction algebra map.  On affine tests this is
185	`DivFamZar` itself (`divFamZarAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its canonical
186	Zariski-continuous extension. -/
187	def divFamZar (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
188	  {s : Π U : T.left.affineOpens, DivFamZar C Γ(T.left, U.1) π n //
189	    ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
190	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
191	
192	namespace divFamZar
193	
194	variable {C π n} {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
195	
196	/-- The compatibility of a section of `divFamZar` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
197	lemma compat (s : divFamZar C π n T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
198	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
199	  s.2 U V h
200	
201	/-- Two sections of `divFamZar` agreeing at every affine open are equal. -/
202	@[ext]
203	lemma ext {s t : divFamZar C π n T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) :
204	    s = t :=
205	  Subtype.ext (funext h)
206	
207	variable (C π n T) in
208	/-- Evaluation of a section of `divFamZar` at an affine open. -/
209	def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : divFamZar C π n T → DivFamZar C Γ(T.left, U.1) π n :=
210	  fun s => s.1 U
211	
212	/-- Evaluation is projection to the component at the affine open. -/
213	@[simp]
214	lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
215	    eval C π n T U s = s.1 U :=
216	  rfl
217	
218	end divFamZar
219	
220	/-! ## The affine comparison -/
221	
222	section Affine
223	
224	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
225	
226	/-- Evaluation at the top affine open of an affine test, composed with the
227	`ΓSpecIso`-transport into the test algebra: the forward direction of the affine
228	comparison. -/
229	def divFamZarToAff : divFamZar C π n (overSpec k R) → DivFamZar C R π n :=
230	  fun s => DivFamZar.congr (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R) (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine R))
231	
232	/-- The section of `divFamZar` over an affine test determined by a locally certified
233	divisor class of the test algebra: restrict from the top affine open — the inverse
234	direction of the affine comparison. -/
235	def divFamZarOfAff : DivFamZar C R π n → divFamZar C π n (overSpec k R) :=
236	  fun x =>
237	    ⟨fun U => DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
238	      ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) le_top).comp
239	        (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom) x,
240	      fun U V h => by rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp, ← AlgHom.comp_assoc,
241	        Over.resAlgHom_comp]⟩
242	
243	/-- The value of `divFamZarOfAff` at every affine open is the restricted transported
244	class. -/
245	lemma divFamZarOfAff_val (x : DivFamZar C R π n) (U : (overSpec k R).left.affineOpens) :
246	    (divFamZarOfAff C π n R x).1 U
247	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
248	          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) le_top).comp
249	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
250	  rfl
251	
252	/-- Round trip on the vehicle side: restricting the transported top value recovers every
253	component, by the compatibility of the section. -/
254	private lemma divFamZarOfAff_divFamZarToAff (s : divFamZar C π n (overSpec k R)) :
255	    divFamZarOfAff C π n R (divFamZarToAff C π n R s) = s := by
256	  refine divFamZar.ext fun U => ?_
257	  calc (divFamZarOfAff C π n R (divFamZarToAff C π n R s)).1 U
258	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
259	          (((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) le_top).comp
260	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom).comp
261	            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom)
262	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine R)) :=
263	        (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp _ _ _).symm
264	    _ = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) le_top)
265	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine R)) := by
266	        rw [AlgHom.comp_assoc,
267	          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom.comp
268	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom
269	            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k R).left, ⊤) from
270	            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm_apply_apply a,
271	          AlgHom.comp_id]
272	    _ = s.1 U := s.compat U (overSpecTopAffine R) le_top
273	
274	/-- Round trip on the algebra side: the two `ΓSpecIso` transports and the trivial
275	restriction collapse to the identity (`DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id`). -/
276	private lemma divFamZarToAff_divFamZarOfAff (x : DivFamZar C R π n) :
277	    divFamZarToAff C π n R (divFamZarOfAff C π n R x) = x := by
278	  calc divFamZarToAff C π n R (divFamZarOfAff C π n R x)
279	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom
280	          ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom.comp
281	            ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) le_top).comp
282	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom)) x :=
283	        (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp _ _ _).symm
284	    _ = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (AlgHom.id k R) x := by
285	        rw [show Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k R) (le_top :
286	              (⊤ : (overSpec k R).left.Opens) ≤ (⊤ : (overSpec k R).left.Opens))
287	            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k R).left, ⊤) from Over.resAlgHom_rfl _ le_top,
288	          AlgHom.id_comp,
289	          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom.comp
290	              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).symm.toAlgHom
291	            = AlgHom.id k R from
292	            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).apply_symm_apply a]
293	    _ = x := DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id x
294	
295	/-- **The affine comparison equivalence** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6, Addendum 2): on
296	an affine test `overSpec k R`, the affine-opens limit `divFamZar` collapses by
297	evaluation at the terminal element `⊤` of the affine-opens poset to the locally
298	certified divisor-functor value `DivFamZar C R π n` of the test algebra (the
299	`divFamAffineEquiv` template). -/
300	def divFamZarAffineEquiv : divFamZar C π n (overSpec k R) ≃ DivFamZar C R π n where
301	  toFun := divFamZarToAff C π n R
302	  invFun := divFamZarOfAff C π n R
303	  left_inv := divFamZarOfAff_divFamZarToAff C π n R
304	  right_inv := divFamZarToAff_divFamZarOfAff C π n R
305	
306	/-- The affine comparison evaluates at the top affine open and transports along
307	`Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv`. -/
308	@[simp]
309	lemma divFamZarAffineEquiv_apply (s : divFamZar C π n (overSpec k R)) :
310	    divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n R s
311	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k R).toAlgHom
312	          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine R)) :=
313	  rfl
314	
315	/-- The inverse affine comparison restricts the transported class from the top affine
316	open. -/
317	@[simp]
318	lemma divFamZarAffineEquiv_symm_apply_val (x : DivFamZar C R π n)
319	    (U : (overSpec k R).left.affineOpens) :
320	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n R).symm x).1 U

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.PiLocalization
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SlicingFlatKernel
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SupportTubeFinite
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertOverlapFinite
10	
11	/-! 
12	# The universal-family certificate assembly
13	
14	This file assembles the seven fields of `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` from the
15	geometric inputs left by the universal-seed construction:
16	
17	* finite chart colengths, supplied by the no-leak theorem in `SupportTubeFinite`;
18	* fibrewise regular chart equations, which make those colengths projective;
19	* a relative submodule spanning the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map;
20	* the fibre dimension of that kernel.
21	
22	The last two inputs feed `SlicingFlatKernel`, simultaneously producing the projective
23	glued module, its constant rank, and both flat-cokernel clauses.  Keeping this assembly
24	generic isolates the remaining DD-4 geometry from the certificate bookkeeping.
25	-/
26	
27	set_option autoImplicit false
28	
29	universe u
30	
31	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
32	open scoped TensorProduct
33	
34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
35	
36	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
37	
38	namespace DivisorAdaptation
39	
40	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
41	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
42	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
43	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
44	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
45	
46	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
47	/-- Assemble a divisor-family certificate from finite regular chart colengths and a
48	submodule which spans the residue-fibre kernels of the Cech difference map.
49	
50	The overlap product is kept as an explicit finite-flat input: producing it from the
51	universal seed is part of the geometric base-change wiring, while all consequences for
52	the certificate are discharged here. -/
53	theorem isCertified_of_kernel_spanning [IsNoetherianRing R] {n : Nat}
54	    (hfin : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
55	    (hregular : forall (j : A.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum R),
56	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
57	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
58	        nonZeroDivisors
59	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
60	    (hovlFinite : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd)
61	    (hovlFlat : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd)
62	    (L : Submodule R A.chartProd)
63	    (hle : L <= LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
64	    (hspan : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
65	      LinearMap.ker ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) <=
66	        LinearMap.range (L.subtype.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
67	    (hdim : forall p : PrimeSpectrum R,
68	      Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
69	          (LinearMap.ker
70	            ((A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight).baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) = n) :
71	    A.IsCertified n := by
72	  letI hfiniteColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := hfin
73	  letI hprojectiveColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Projective R (A.colength j) :=
74	    fun j => A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hregular j)
75	  letI hflatColength : forall j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) :=
76	    fun j => A.flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j (hregular j)
77	  letI hfiniteChart : Module.Finite R A.chartProd := Module.Finite.pi
78	  letI hflatChart : Module.Flat R A.chartProd := Module.Flat.pi_of_finite
79	  letI hfiniteOvl : Module.Finite R A.ovlProd := hovlFinite
80	  letI hflatOvl : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd := hovlFlat
81	  have hfiniteGlued : Module.Finite R A.Glued :=

11	
12	DDR-9.F7 has two logically separate parts: lifting the affine equivalences to arbitrary
13	tests, and packaging the resulting natural equivalences as a `RepresentableBy` datum.
14	This file formalizes the second part.  `DivRepGlobalData` records the general-test
15	pullback, classification map, inverse laws, and naturality.  Its `representableBy`
16	constructor is the final categorical packaging.
17	
18	The affine-to-general lift is intentionally not assumed to exist implicitly: a caller
19	must provide every field of `DivRepGlobalData`.

66	construction, `pull` is assembled from the affine forward maps and `classify` by
67	gluing the affine backward classifiers. -/
68	structure DivRepGlobalData where
69	  pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
70	    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
71	  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
72	    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)
73	  classify_pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
74	    classify (pull v) = v
75	  pull_classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T),
76	    pull (classify F) = F

78	    (v : T ⟶ DivOver),

91	  right_inv := D.pull_classify

98	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T v

128	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv v = D.pull v :=
129	  rfl

136	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
137	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv.symm F = D.classify F :=

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivCarveLocus
7	
8	/-!
9	# `DivScheme g = Z(♦)`: the carve locus as a closed subscheme of the Grassmannian pair (DDR-1)
10	
11	The glued carve locus of the DAT-D design (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 1): the
12	chart-wise loci `Z(♦) ⊆ Spec (R^I ⊗ R^J)` (`Picard/DivCarveLocus.lean`) assemble into a
13	closed subscheme of `grPair` through the mathlib ideal-sheaf machinery — `carveIdealSheaf`
14	is the kernel ideal sheaf of the disjoint family of chart loci (the largest ideal sheaf
15	vanishing on all of them, `⨅ over the pair atlas`), and `DivScheme` is its subscheme.
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveIdealSheaf`: the ideal sheaf `I_♦` on `grPair`.
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme`, `carveSchemeι`, `carveSchemeOver`: the generic glued
19	  locus, its closed immersion (mathlib's `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` instance), and its
20	  `Over (Spec k)` form.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker` and
22	  `carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors`: the factoring criterion at chart tests — a test
23	  map through a pair chart killing the chart carve ideal factors (uniquely, by `Mono`)
24	  through `carveSchemeι`.
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.carveScheme_hom_ext` (`divScheme_hom_ext`, DDR-7's tail): morphisms
26	  into the locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion.
27	* **Campaign spellings**: `DivScheme`, `divSchemeι`, `divSchemeOver` at the DAT-D
28	  windows.
29	
30	The chart-value identification (`carveIdealSheaf.ideal (pair chart) = I_♦`-chart, the
31	`KeyChart` of the DD-R roadmap) rests on the landed gluing compatibility
32	(`carveIdeal_le_ker_of_specMap_pairChartMap_eq`); its remaining half is the app-level
33	localization bookkeeping and is left to the successor lane (see the inbox memory).
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open TensorProduct CategoryTheory
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	open Grassmannian
45	
46	section Generic
47	
48	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
49	variable {ι : Type u} (μ : ι → ((Fin r₁ → k) →ₗ[k] (Fin r₂ → k)))
50	
51	/-- **The carve ideal sheaf `I_♦`** on the Grassmannian pair: the largest ideal sheaf
52	vanishing on every chart-wise carve locus — the infimum of the kernels of the chart
53	loci mapped into `grPair`. -/
54	noncomputable def carveIdealSheaf : (grPair k g r₁ g r₂).IdealSheafData :=
55	  ⨅ c : (glueData k g r₁).J × (glueData k g r₂).J,
56	    (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ c.1 c.2).ker
57	
58	/-- **The glued carve locus `Z(♦)`** as a scheme: the subscheme of the carve ideal
59	sheaf on the Grassmannian pair. -/
60	noncomputable def carveScheme : Scheme :=
61	  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subscheme
62	
63	/-- **The closed immersion `Z(♦) ⟶ grPair`**. -/
64	noncomputable def carveSchemeι : carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂ :=
65	  (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι
66	
67	instance isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι :
68	    IsClosedImmersion (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) :=
69	  inferInstanceAs (IsClosedImmersion (carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ).subschemeι)
70	
71	/-- The kernel of the closed immersion is the carve ideal sheaf. -/
72	theorem ker_carveSchemeι :
73	    (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ).ker = carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ :=
74	  Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι _
75	
76	/-- **`Z(♦)` as a test object of `Over (Spec k)`**. -/
77	noncomputable def carveSchemeOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
78	  Over.mk (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ ≫ grPairStructMap k g r₁ g r₂)
79	
80	/-- Each chart-wise carve locus maps to the glued locus over `grPair`. -/
81	theorem carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_carveLocusToGrPair
82	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
83	    carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ ≤ (carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j).ker :=
84	  iInf_le _ (i, j)
85	
86	/-- **The factoring criterion, existence half** (the chart-test universal property): a
87	test morphism through a pair chart whose chart map kills the chart carve ideal factors
88	through the closed immersion `carveSchemeι`. -/
89	theorem carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker
90	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
91	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
92	    (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →+* S)
93	    (hker : carveIdeal k g r₁ r₂ μ i j ≤ RingHom.ker w) :
94	    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ,
95	      v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ
96	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j := by
97	  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, -⟩ := (ideal_le_ker_iff_factors _ w).mp hker
98	  have hfac : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j
99	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j := by
100	    rw [carveLocusToGrPair, carveLocusι]
101	    refine Eq.trans ?_ (Category.assoc _ _ _)
102	    refine congrArg (· ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j) ?_
103	    rw [← Spec.map_comp]
104	    exact (congrArg (fun ρ => Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ρ)) hφ).symm
105	  refine ⟨IsClosedImmersion.lift (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ)
106	    (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j) ?_,
107	    IsClosedImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _⟩
108	  rw [ker_carveSchemeι, hfac]
109	  exact le_trans (carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_carveLocusToGrPair k g r₁ r₂ μ i j)
110	    (Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp _ _)
111	
112	/-- **The factoring criterion, kernel half**: a test morphism factoring through the
113	closed immersion has the carve ideal sheaf in its kernel. -/
114	theorem carveIdealSheaf_le_ker_of_factors {T : Scheme.{u}} (u : T ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂)
115	    (v : T ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ) (hv : v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ = u) :
116	    carveIdealSheaf k g r₁ r₂ μ ≤ u.ker := by
117	  rw [← hv, ← ker_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ]
118	  exact Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp _ _
119	
120	/-- **Hom-ext into `Z(♦)`** (the `divScheme_hom_ext` tail of DDR-7): morphisms into the
121	glued carve locus are determined by their composites with the closed immersion — closed
122	immersions are monomorphisms. -/
123	theorem carveScheme_hom_ext {T : Scheme.{u}} (u v : T ⟶ carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ μ)
124	    (h : u ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ = v ≫ carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ) : u = v :=
125	  (cancel_mono (carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ μ)).mp h
126	
127	end Generic
128	
129	/-! ## The campaign spellings (the DAT-D windows) -/
130	
131	section Curve
132	
133	open Scheme
134	
135	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
136	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
137	variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
138	variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
139	variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
140	
141	/-- **`DivScheme g = Z(♦)`** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 1): the glued carve locus
142	of the DAT-D two-window multiplication carve, a closed subscheme of the Grassmannian
143	pair `Gr(g, H_M) ×_k Gr(g, H_{M+s})` through `divSchemeι`. -/
144	noncomputable def DivScheme : Scheme :=
145	  carveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
146	
147	/-- **The closed immersion `divSchemeι : DivScheme g ⟶ grPair`**. -/
148	noncomputable def divSchemeι : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ grPair k g r₁ g r₂ :=
149	  carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
150	
151	instance isClosedImmersion_divSchemeι :
152	    IsClosedImmersion (divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :=
153	  isClosedImmersion_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
154	
155	/-- **`DivScheme g` as a test object of `Over (Spec k)`**. -/
156	noncomputable def divSchemeOver : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
157	  carveSchemeOver k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
158	
159	/-- The DDR-1 factoring criterion at the campaign windows: a chart test killing `I_♦`
160	factors through `divSchemeι`. -/
161	theorem divScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker
162	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
163	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →+* S)
164	    (hker : divCarveIdeal k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≤ RingHom.ker w) :
165	    ∃ v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
166	      v ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
167	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
168	  carveScheme_exists_factor_of_le_ker k g r₁ r₂ _ i j w hker
169	
170	/-- **`divScheme_hom_ext`** (DDR-7): morphisms into `DivScheme g` are determined by
171	their composites with `divSchemeι`. -/
172	theorem divScheme_hom_ext {T : Scheme.{u}} (u v : T ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
173	    (h : u ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ = v ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
174	    u = v :=
175	  carveScheme_hom_ext k g r₁ r₂ _ u v h
176	
177	end Curve
178	
179	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# Locally certified divisor families: the `DivFamZar` carrier (DD-2 stage S5b)
12	
13	The Addendum-2 repair of the divisor-functor carrier (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`,
14	Addendum 2): the globally-certified `DivFam` is not a Zariski sheaf — the diagonal
15	divisor over `Γ(C \ pt)` is certifiable on a basic-open cover of the base but carries
16	no global certificate — so the faithful functor value is the **locally certified**
17	quotient `DivFamZar`. The generic germ-regularity engines live in
18	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit`.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertified` — the Addendum-2 frozen pin: a span-⊤ family
21	  `g : Fin m → R` with certified divisor families over `Localization.Away (g i)`
22	  divisor-equal to the pulled system; `hreg` is discharged by the Kit's open-immersion
23	  lemma, with the S4 instance provided by `haveI`.
24	* `IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq` — the pin respects divisor equality.
25	* `CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified` — a global certificate is a local one
26	  (trivial cover `g = ![1]`; the certified part is `mapAlg` to `Localization.Away 1`,
27	  whose equations ARE the pulled system on the nose).
28	* `IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the mapAlg-hreg
29	  engine**: a locally certified system has regular pulled equations along the
30	  comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'` — regularity is germ-local, each germ
31	  sits over a chart `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` of `R'`, where the
32	  local certificate's regularity transports through its `DivEq` and the landed
33	  certificate-based pullback regularity.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar` — the quotient of locally certified systems by
35	  `DivEq`, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `picClass`, and `DivFam.toZar`.
36	
37	Total `DivFamZar.mapAlg` and the Zariski keystones are
38	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg` / `…ZarGlue`.
39	-/

41	set_option autoImplicit false
42	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C R, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
43	`(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/
44	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

52	open Opposite

55	
56	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
57	
58	/-! ## The locally certified pin -/
59	
60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
61	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
62	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]
63	
64	/-- **The Addendum-2 frozen pin** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): a
65	local-equation system on the relative curve is *locally certified* in degree `n` if
66	some span-⊤ family `g : Fin m → R` carries certified divisor families over the
67	localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` that are divisor-equal to the pulled system.
68	The pullback's regularity hypothesis is discharged once and for all by the Kit's
69	open-immersion lemma — the comparison of an away localization is an open immersion
70	(the S4 instance, provided by `haveI`). -/
71	def IsLocallyCertified (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
72	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
73	    ∀ i : Fin m,
74	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
75	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
76	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) π n,
77	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
78	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
79	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
80	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))

82	variable {C R π}

84	/-- **The locally certified pin respects divisor equality**: the local `DivEq`s
85	transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
86	theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
87	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
88	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
89	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
90	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
91	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
92	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
93	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
94	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
95	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
96	      h _ _)⟩
97	
98	/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
99	certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
100	equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
101	the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
102	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
103	    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
104	  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
105	  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
106	    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
107	  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
108	      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
109	    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
110	      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩

114	section MapAlgHreg
115	
116	variable {n : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
117	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']

120	equations along the comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'`. Regularity is
121	germ-local on the curve: the charts `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` cover
122	`relCurve C R'` by open immersions; over each, the composite comparison factors
123	through the certified chart `Localization.Away (g i)`, where the certificate's
124	pullback regularity (`DivisorAdaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`)
125	transports through the recorded `DivEq`. -/
126	theorem IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
127	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
128	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
129	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
130	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
131	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
132	  classical
133	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
134	  -- the away charts of `R'` at the pushed cover, and their immersions
135	  haveI himm : ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin m),
136	      IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R'
137	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) := fun i =>
138	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R'
139	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
140	  -- the pushed family spans the unit ideal of `R'`
141	  have hspan' : Ideal.span (Set.range
142	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) = ⊤ := by
143	    have hrange : Set.range (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
144	        = algebraMap R R' '' Set.range g := by
145	      ext x
146	      constructor
147	      · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
148	        exact ⟨g i.down, ⟨i.down, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
149	      · rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
150	        exact ⟨⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
151	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
152	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_immersion_cover
153	    (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => relCurveMap C R'
154	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))
155	    (fun y' => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R'
156	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
157	      (fun i => Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) hspan' y')
158	    (relCurveMap C R R') d (fun i ζ => ?_) y z hz
159	  -- over the chart at `g i`: factor the composite through the certified localization
160	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i.down
161	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) :=
162	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i.down)) (g i.down)
163	  -- the away map `Localization.Away (g i) → Localization.Away (φ (g i))` as an
164	  -- algebra tower
165	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i.down))
166	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
167	    (IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers (g i.down))
168	      (T := Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
169	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R')
170	      (by
171	        rintro x ⟨e, rfl⟩
172	        use e
173	        simp)).toAlgebra
174	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
175	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
176	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
177	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, IsLocalization.map_comp,
178	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq])
179	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (g i.down))
180	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
181	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
182	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R (Localization.Away (g i.down)),
183	        ← RingHom.comp_assoc,
184	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
185	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))),
186	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R
187	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))])
188	  -- the comparison triangle through the two factorizations of `C_{T i} → C_R`
189	  have hcomp₁ : relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
190	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
191	      ≫ relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
192	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
193	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away (g i.down))
194	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
195	  have hcomp₂ : relCurveMap C R' (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
196	      ≫ relCurveMap C R R'
197	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
198	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := R')
199	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
200	  have step1 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_congr hcomp₂ d ζ
201	  have step2 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_comp hcomp₁ d
202	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
203	      (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) d) ζ
204	  have hfinal := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_self_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_divEq
205	    (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
206	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) hGdiv ζ
207	    (G.adaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
208	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
209	      G.certified.projective_colength ζ ζ
210	      ((G.eqns.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
211	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))).mem_opens ζ))
212	  exact ((step1.trans step2).symm ▸ hfinal)
213	
214	end MapAlgHreg

216	/-! ## The locally certified divisor-functor value -/
217	
218	variable (C R π)
219	variable (n : ℕ)
220	
221	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on locally certified systems (Addendum 2's mirror of
222	`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
223	certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
224	def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
225	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
226	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
227	  iseqv :=
228	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
229	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
230	
231	/-- **The locally certified divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`**
232	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
233	degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
234	a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
235	def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
236	
237	namespace DivFamZar
238	
239	variable {C R π n}
240	
241	/-- The class of a locally certified system. -/
242	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
243	    DivFamZar C R π n :=
244	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩
245	
246	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
247	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₂} :
248	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
249	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
250	
251	/-- **The Picard class of a locally certified divisor class** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on
252	the quotient by `picClass_eq_of_divEq`. -/
253	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
254	  Quotient.lift
255	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>
256	      d.1.picClass)
257	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
258	
259	@[simp]
260	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
261	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
262	  rfl
263	
264	end DivFamZar
265	
266	variable {C R π n}
267	
268	/-- **The comparison from the globally certified value**: a certified family is
269	locally certified (trivial cover), and divisor equality is the relation on both
270	sides. Over a field the two notions agree; over a general base `toZar` is the
271	sheafification-of-value comparison. -/
272	def DivFam.toZar : DivFam C R π n → DivFamZar C R π n :=
273	  Quotient.lift
274	    (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n =>
275	      DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified)
276	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr h)
277	
278	@[simp]
279	lemma DivFam.toZar_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
280	    (DivFam.mk F).toZar = DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified :=
281	  rfl
282	
283	/-- The Picard class factors through `toZar`. -/
284	@[simp]
285	lemma DivFamZar.picClass_toZar (F : DivFam C R π n) :
286	    F.toZar.picClass = F.picClass := by
287	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
288	  | h F => rfl
289	
290	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarSwallow

/-!
# A connected divisor can be certified only inside a single pinned chart

The two preceding files bracket the certificate assembler's per-piece no-leak clause:
`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows it forces the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to
be closed, and `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` shows the "swallow or miss" shape produces it.
This file closes the bracket, and thereby decides the lane's satisfiability question.

The observation is that leak-freeness *plus connectedness of the divisor* already implies
swallow-or-miss.  For each piece the trace `supportLocus ∩ pieces j` is open in the support
(the piece is open) and closed in it (that is leak-freeness), so a connected support leaves
only the two degenerate values: the trace is empty, or it is everything.  Feeding this into
the chart dichotomies of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` and `relCover_sup` gives

> **a nonempty connected divisor whose adaptation is leak-free at every piece lies inside
> `V₀` or inside `V₁`.**

That is the satisfiability verdict the lane never obtained.  It is not a statement about
pieces, adaptations, tubes or fibres: it says the certificate interface can only ever be
satisfied by divisors confined to one pinned chart of `pi` — a **chart-design** condition.

Nor can a shrink of the base repair it, because base localization does not disconnect the
divisor: `Spec (R[x]/(x² − t))` over `R = k[t]` is connected over every basic open of
`Spec R`, so no Zariski neighbourhood of `t = 0` splits the divisor into clopen packets.
Hence the "clopen packet extraction" programme (memory I-0209) is available exactly when the
divisor is already chart-confined, and the honest obligation of the lane is to make the
DD-R atlas produce chart-confined divisors.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak` —
  leak-freeness at a piece plus a connected support forces swallow-or-miss at that piece.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected` — the
  same for every piece at once, i.e. leak-free + connected ⟹ swallow-or-miss.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected` — **the
  satisfiability verdict**: a nonempty connected support with a leak-free adaptation lies
  inside one of the two pinned charts.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected` —
  the contrapositive obstruction: a connected divisor meeting both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)`
  admits no adaptation with a leak-free piece.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

/-! ## Connectedness turns leak-freeness into swallow-or-miss -/

/-- **A connected support leaves a leak-free piece no middle ground.** The trace
`supportLocus ∩ pieces j` is open in the support because the piece is open, and closed in it
because nothing leaks; a preconnected support therefore has the trace empty or total.

Stated with `IsPreconnected` on the ambient set (rather than `ConnectedSpace` on the
subtype) so that no coercion bookkeeping is needed: the two separating opens are the piece
itself and the complement of the — closed — trace. -/
theorem subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak (j : A.index)
    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
    (hleak : d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
    d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
  classical
  have hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :=
    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mpr hleak
  -- the two separating opens: the piece, and the complement of the (closed) trace
  by_cases hdisj : Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
  · exact Or.inr hdisj
  refine Or.inl ?_
  by_contra hnsub
  -- both halves are nonempty, so preconnectedness produces a point in their intersection
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := Set.not_disjoint_iff.mp hdisj
  obtain ⟨y, hyS, hyU⟩ := Set.not_subset.mp hnsub
  obtain ⟨z, hzS, hzu, hzv⟩ :=
    hconn (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
      (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))ᶜ
      (A.pieces j).isOpen hclosed.isOpen_compl
      (fun w hw => by
        by_cases hwU : w ∈ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
        · exact Or.inl hwU
        · exact Or.inr fun hc => hwU hc.2)
      ⟨x, hx.1, hx.2⟩ ⟨y, hyS, fun hc => hyU hc.2⟩
  exact hzv ⟨hzS, hzu⟩

/-- **Leak-free at every piece plus a connected support ⟹ swallow-or-miss.** So the
hypothesis of `forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` is not an extra assumption for a
connected divisor: it is what leak-freeness already says. -/
theorem forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected
    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
    (hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
    ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := fun j =>
  A.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak j hconn (hleak j)

/-! ## The satisfiability verdict -/

/-- **A nonempty connected divisor with a leak-free adaptation lies inside one pinned
chart.** The verdict the certificate lane needed: since `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` (`relCover_sup`), the
two chart dichotomies of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` cannot both land on their `Disjoint`
branch for a nonempty support.

Consequently the certificate interface `IsCertified` — whose per-piece clause (c1) forces
leak-freeness — is satisfiable for a connected divisor **only** if that divisor avoids
`pi⁻¹(∞)` (so it sits in `V₀`) or avoids `pi⁻¹(0)` (so it sits in `V₁`).  This is a
condition on the divisor and the chosen `pi`; the adaptation, the support tube, the packet
idempotents and the base shrink are all irrelevant to it. -/
theorem supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected
    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus) (hne : d.supportLocus.Nonempty)
    (hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
      ∨ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
  have hswallow := A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected hconn hleak
  rcases A.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀ hswallow with h₀ | h₀
  · exact Or.inl h₀
  -- the support misses `V₀`, so `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` puts all of it in `V₁`
  refine Or.inr fun x hx => ?_
  have hmem : x ∈ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) := by
    rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
  rcases (Opens.mem_sup ..).mp hmem with h | h
  · exact absurd rfl (by simpa using Set.disjoint_left.mp h₀ hx h)
  · exact h

/-- **The obstruction.** A nonempty connected divisor lying in neither pinned chart — i.e.
meeting both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — admits **no** adaptation that is leak-free at every
piece, hence no certificate, over any base and after any shrink.

Model to keep in mind: the degree-two relative divisor `V(t x² + x y + t y²) ⊆ ℙ¹` over
`k[t]`, whose section ring is a domain (so it is connected over every basic open of
`Spec k[t]`) and whose fibre at `t = 0` is `{0, ∞}`. -/
theorem not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected
    (hconn : IsPreconnected d.supportLocus) (hne : d.supportLocus.Nonempty)
    (h₀ : ¬ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
    (h₁ : ¬ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    ¬ ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := fun hleak =>
  (A.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected hconn hne hleak).elim h₀ h₁

end DivisorAdaptation

end AlgebraicGeometry

11	/-!
12	# Certified divisor families: the DD-1 carrier (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1)
13	
14	The Wave-4 DAT-D divisor functor's object data over an affine test `R`, the worksheet's
15	(D1) pin (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §1.1): a `LocalEquations` system `d` on the
16	relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R`, a **finite chart adaptation** refining it — finitely
17	many basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts with partition witnesses, carrying
18	regular equations `f_j` that agree with `d`'s equations up to units — and the **colength
19	certificate**: the chart-local colength modules `Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)` are finite projective
20	over `R`, and the glued equalizer module `W(d)` is finite projective of constant fibre
21	rank `n` (`Module.rankAtStalk`), with the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
22	certificates base-change (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`).
23	
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData` — the `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data (`Type u`;
25	  DAT-1's `BasicOpenCoverData` shape is `Type (u+1)`, unusable inside a functor value).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation` — the adaptation: equations + the pointwise
27	  refinement-up-to-units clause `eqn_rel` (point-free, so it pulls back along arbitrary
28	  morphisms), with the anchored constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`.
29	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule` — the glued colength module
30	  `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺) ⊆ Π_j Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)`, with the equalizer description
31	  `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` (the worksheet's `eq(∏_j ⇉ ∏_{j,j'})`).
32	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` — the certificate (c1)–(c4).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq` — divisor equality of local-equation
34	  systems: on a common refinement the equations agree up to units (refinement +
35	  rescaling in one move), an equivalence relation with
36	  `picClass_eq_of_divEq` (the class laws `picClass_restrict`/`picClass_rescale`).
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily`, `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFam` — the certified
38	  family and the setoid quotient `DivFam C π n R : Type u`, the divisor functor's value
39	  on the affine test `R`, with `DivFam.picClass`.
40	
41	The `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through
42	`relCurve.instOver` (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate the same

64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
69	
70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
79	
80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
82	
83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
89	
90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by

227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):

229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of

231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
