243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
246	
247	namespace DivisorAdaptation
248	
249	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
250	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
251	
252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
265	  toFinCoverData := D
266	  eqn := eqn
267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
289	            from rfl]
290	          exact E1
291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
299	          rw [E2]
300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
305	          rw [mul_assoc]
306	
307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
323	    exact h
324	  rw [hgerm]
325	  exact mul_mem
326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))
329	
330	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
331	
332	/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
333	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
334	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
335	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
336	
337	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
339	through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
340	DEFINITION. -/
341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
343	  Ideal.span
344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
346	
347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
348	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
350	
351	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
352	the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
353	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
356	    (by
357	      intro a ha
358	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
366	
367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
371	    (by
372	      intro a ha
373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
381	
382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
385	
386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
388	
389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
391	  LinearMap.pi
392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
393	
394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
396	  LinearMap.pi
397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
398	
399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
405	
406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
414	
415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
417	
418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442	
443	end DivisorAdaptation
444	
445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)
448	
449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
459	
460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
468	
469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)
473	
474	namespace DivFam
475	
476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
477	
478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
485	
486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)

96	/-- Two unit Čech cocycles on a pointed cover are cohomologous if a `0`-cochain of unit
97	sections conjugates their pair values into each other. -/
98	lemma unitsCocycle_isCohomologous {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} {γ δ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰}
99	    (α : ∀ i, Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ)
100	    (h : ∀ i j, X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left (α i) * unitsEvInf γ i j
101	      = unitsEvInf δ i j * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (α j)) :
102	    γ.IsCohomologous δ :=
103	  (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf γ δ).mpr ⟨α, h⟩

105	/-! ## Local equations -/
106	
107	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor on `X`, adapted to a pointed cover:
108	a section `eqn x` on each member `cover.opens x`, whose germ at every point of that member
109	is a nonzerodivisor (`regular`) and whose overlap ratios `eqn x / eqn y` are units
110	(`ratio_isUnit`). The class of the associated Čech cocycle of transition units is the
111	divisor class `𝒪(D)`, see `LocalEquations.picClass`. -/
112	structure LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
113	  /-- The pointed cover on whose members the local equations live. -/
114	  cover : X.PointedCover
115	  /-- The local equation on the member `cover.opens x`. -/
116	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
117	  /-- Each local equation is regular: its germ at every point of its member is a
118	  nonzerodivisor in the stalk. This is the primitive form of regularity; it implies the
119	  regularity of every restriction (`eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). -/
120	  regular : ∀ (x y : X) (hy : y ∈ cover.opens x),
121	    (X.presheaf.germ (cover.opens x) y hy).hom (eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)
122	  /-- On the overlap `cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y` the two equations differ by a unit
123	  factor `eqn x = u · eqn y`, so that `𝒪(D)` is invertible. -/
124	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, ∃ u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y)ˣ,
125	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn x)
126	      = (u : Γ(X, cover.opens x ⊓ cover.opens y))
127	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (eqn y)
128	
129	namespace LocalEquations
130	
131	variable (d : X.LocalEquations)
132	
133	/-- Section-level regularity: the restriction of `eqn x` to any sub-open `W ≤ cover.opens x`
134	is a nonzerodivisor in `Γ(X, W)`. Sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their
135	germs, so nonzerodivisibility of the germs (the field `regular`) propagates to every
136	restriction. -/
137	lemma eqn_restrict_mem_nonZeroDivisors (x : X) {W : X.Opens} (hW : W ≤ d.cover.opens x) :
138	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x) ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
139	  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
140	  intro t ht
141	  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
142	  intro y hy
143	  rw [map_zero]
144	  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t
145	      * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op).hom (d.eqn x)) = 0 := by
146	    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
147	  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at key
148	  exact (mul_left_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (d.regular x y (hW hy))).mp
149	    (by rw [mul_comm] at key; exact key)
150	
151	/-! ## The transition units -/
152	
153	/-- The transition unit `g x y = eqn x / eqn y ∈ Γ(X, 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)ˣ`: the unique unit with
154	`eqn x|∩ = g x y · eqn y|∩`. -/
155	noncomputable def ratioUnit (x y : X) : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ :=
156	  (d.ratio_isUnit x y).choose
157	
158	/-- The defining property of the transition unit `g x y`: on the overlap,
159	`eqn x = g x y · eqn y`. -/
160	lemma eqn_restrict_eq (x y : X) :
161	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d.eqn x)
162	      = (d.ratioUnit x y : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
163	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y) :=
164	  (d.ratio_isUnit x y).choose_spec

20	(`isClosed_supportLocus`); for a missing piece the trace is empty.  Neither case needs a
21	fibre, a tube, or an idempotent.
22	
23	The crudeness is not a defect, because the necessity lemma pins down exactly how much
24	freedom is left.  Both pinned charts are covered by their pieces, so
25	
26	* if some chart-`b` piece meets the support it must swallow it, whence `supportLocus ⊆ V_b`;
27	* otherwise every chart-`b` piece misses the support, whence `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ∅`.
28	
29	Since `V₀ ⊔ V₁` is the whole relative curve, a nonempty support therefore lies in
30	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the divisor must avoid **both** vertical fibres `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — or be
31	confined to one of them.  That is the honest chart-design hypothesis of the lane, and it is
32	where the DD-R atlas has to do its work; it is not something a support tube, a packet
33	idempotent, or a shrink of the base can manufacture.
34	
35	A missing piece contributes nothing at all: its equation is a unit, so its colength module
36	vanishes (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`) and clauses (c1) hold there for
37	free — no fibrewise regularity input.  So the certificate of a swallow-or-miss adaptation is
38	carried entirely by the swallowing pieces, at most one per chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a
43	  piece missing the support has a vanishing colength.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — swallow
45	  or miss gives no-leak at that piece.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` — the
47	  assembler-shaped `hnoLeak`, with no fibre analysis.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` —
49	  clause (c1)-finite at every piece.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` /
51	  `…_chart₁_…` — the design constraint the shape imposes on the divisor.
52	-/

63	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

65	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

67	namespace DivisorAdaptation
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
71	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
72	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
73	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
74	
75	/-! ## A piece missing the support contributes nothing -/
76	
77	/-- **A piece that misses the support has a vanishing colength.** Its equation has a unit
78	germ at every point of the piece (`isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` read through the unit locus), hence
79	is a unit (`RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), hence spans the unit ideal.
80	
81	This is the colength companion of `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`: on
82	such a piece the certificate's clauses (c1) are free, with no fibrewise regularity input. -/
83	lemma subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (j : A.index)
84	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
85	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) := by
86	  have hunit : IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
87	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
88	    intro z hz
89	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
90	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hz).mpr
91	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
92	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr
93	    (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span rfl) hunit)
94	
95	/-! ## Swallow or miss gives no-leak -/
96	
97	/-- **Swallow or miss gives no-leak at that piece.** If the piece contains the whole support
98	its trace is the support, closed by `isClosed_supportLocus`; if the piece misses the support
99	its trace is empty.  In neither case is a fibre, a tube or an idempotent involved. -/
100	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint (j : A.index)
101	    (h : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
102	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
103	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
104	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
105	  rcases h with hsub | hdisj
106	  · rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
107	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus
108	  · rw [Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hdisj]
109	    exact isClosed_empty
110	
111	/-- **The assembler-shaped `hnoLeak` from swallow-or-miss.** This is the hypothesis of
112	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` /
113	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` /
114	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`, produced with no fibre analysis. -/
115	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
116	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
117	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
118	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
119	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
120	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
121	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
122	  intro j s x hx
123	  have hleak := A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j)
124	  by_contra hxU
125	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hleak x ⟨hx.2, hxU⟩
126	
127	section Finite
128	
129	/- The finiteness engine consumes the properness licence on the relative curve
130	(`instIsProperRelCurveHom`), so this clause — and only this clause — needs `IsProper`. -/
131	variable [IsProper C.hom]
132	
133	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite at every piece, from swallow-or-miss.** -/
134	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
135	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
136	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
137	    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := fun j =>
138	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
139	    (A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j))
140	
141	end Finite
142	
143	/-! ## What the shape forces on the divisor
144	
145	The necessity direction of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` is sharpened here: because the
146	chart-`b` pieces cover `V_b`, a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor that is
147	either inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it.  Combined with `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` this says a
148	nonempty support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, or is confined to one vertical fibre of `pi`.
149	
150	This is the statement the DD-R atlas owes: **the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and
151	`pi⁻¹(∞)`.**  It is a hypothesis about the chart, and it is the only remaining geometric
152	input of the (c1) side of the certificate. -/
153	
154	/-- **Chart-0 dichotomy.** A swallow-or-miss adaptation forces the support either inside the
155	pinned chart `V₀` or disjoint from it. -/
156	theorem subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀
157	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
158	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
161	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
162	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R))
163	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
164	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx)
165	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
166	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
167	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
168	    exact (h (Sum.inl j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
169	
170	/-- **Chart-1 dichotomy.** -/
171	theorem subset_chart₁_or_disjoint_chart₁
172	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
173	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
174	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
175	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
176	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
177	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R))
178	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
179	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx)
180	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
181	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
182	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
183	    exact (h (Sum.inr j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
184	
185	end DivisorAdaptation
186	
187	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	# The chart trace is what no-leak really asks for
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise no-leak clause, which is
13	emptiness of the leak locus, which is closedness of the piece trace
14	`supportLocus ∩ pieces j` (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`), which
15	is clopen-ness of that trace inside the support (`isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`).

18	**the per-piece clause cannot be produced piece by piece.**  A `FinCoverData` carries a
19	partition of unity on each pinned chart, so the chart-`b` pieces cover the *whole* pinned
20	chart `V_b` — hence the union of their traces is the whole chart trace
21	`supportLocus ∩ V_b`.  A finite union of closed sets is closed, so
22	
23	> no-leak at every chart-`b` piece **forces** `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed in the
24	> relative curve, i.e. the chart trace to be clopen in the support.
25	
26	That is a property of the *system and the pinned charts alone*: no choice of adaptation, and
27	no shrinking of the base, can produce no-leak for a system whose chart trace is not closed.
28	It is therefore the honest gate of the lane, and it replaces the refuted `tube-fibre`
29	framing (put the support inside one piece — impossible once the support meets both charts,
30	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`) and the refuted separated framing
31	(`DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`) with a single geometric statement about the divisor.

33	Read positively, it also says where to aim: `supportLocus ∩ V₀` and `supportLocus ∩ V₁`
34	closed is not merely necessary, it is *sufficient*, because the two-piece adaptation whose
35	pieces are the pinned charts themselves realizes it (`DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`).

42	  and its chart-1 twin — no-leak at every piece of a chart forces the chart trace closed.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak` —
44	  the assembler-shaped form: the `hnoLeak` hypothesis of
45	  `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` forces both chart traces closed.

113	    (h : ∀ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLeak (A.pieces (Sum.inr j)) = ∅) :

116	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]

118	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty _).mpr (h j)

122	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` (equivalently of

124	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`) implies a statement that mentions
125	neither the adaptation nor its pieces — only the system and the two pinned charts. -/
126	theorem isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak
127	    (hnoLeak : ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
128	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
129	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
130	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
131	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
132	        ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
133	      ∧ IsClosed (d.supportLocus
134	        ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
135	  have hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := fun j =>

154	theorem not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀

160	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=

166	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
167	    ¬ ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
168	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
169	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
170	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
171	  fun h => hnc (A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak h).2

/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

12	/-!
13	# DD-4 RelDivisor (Route 2) — the relative-local base-point-free Nakayama neighbourhood
14	
15	The load-bearing algebraic engine of the divisor-first relative achiever
16	(`informal/spec-dd4-seam.md` §2.3, landing note I-0268): the **flat ⟹
17	module-fibre-zero = scheme-fibre-zero, so its support avoids `p`; shrink to the
18	support-free neighbourhood** step that turns a *fibre* achiever into a *relative*
19	generator.
20	
21	Route 2 (I-0268) builds the relative effective Cartier divisor `d` over the chart ring
22	`R_Z` directly from the universal carve's flat rank-`g` quotient, and reads off the seed
23	fields `(side z, h z, sec z)`. The residual honest step is **relative local
24	base-point-freeness**: for each `z`, on a small enough `D(h z)`, the chosen `sec z ∈
25	K_univ` generates the Cartier ideal `I_d`. Fibrewise this is P-fib's achiever; the
26	relative lift is a *Nakayama-neighbourhood*:
27	
28	* the colength `Q := I_d ⧸ (sec z)` is a **finite** `R_Z`-module (finiteness from
29	  `SupportTubeFinite`, I-0244);
30	* because `I_d` is the **flat** Cartier ideal (§2.2; the flatness of the colength is what
31	  makes the *module* fibre agree with the *scheme* fibre — supplied by
32	  `SlicingFlatKernel`, I-0240, and the flat-cokernel base-change engine
33	  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`), the fibre achiever `f_p` gives
34	  `Q ⊗ κ(p) = 0` genuinely — *not* mere fibrewise vanishing;
35	* hence the support of `Q` avoids `p`, and shrinking `D(h z)` to that support-free
36	  neighbourhood makes `sec z` generate `I_d` there.
37	
38	**This file supplies the last bullet's engine** (`Module.exists_subsingleton_away_of_*`):
39	for a finite `R`-module `Q` whose residue-field fibre at `p` vanishes, some `f ∉ p`
40	localizes `Q` to zero — the honest "support avoids `p`; shrink the neighbourhood" move.
41	
42	**I-0231 / `k[ε]` guard.** The hypothesis is the *module* fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p) = 0`, **not**
43	"vanishes in every fibre". For the bad section (`e = t+ε`, `K`-components `(t)`, over
44	`R = k[ε]`) the colength `Q = (ε)` has `Q ⊗_{k[ε]} k ≅ k ≠ 0` (§2.1), so the hypothesis
45	*correctly fails* and the engine cannot certify it — exactly the guard the `k[ε]`
46	counterexample enforces. The engine is applicable only once the flat Cartier structure
47	(§2.2) has genuinely produced `Q ⊗ κ(p) = 0`, which is where flatness (not fibrewise
48	vanishing) does the work.
49	-/

61	/-- **Relative-local BPF Nakayama neighbourhood** (`spec-dd4-seam` §2.3, residue field on
62	the left): if the residue-field fibre `κ(p) ⊗ M` of a **finite** `R`-module `M` at a prime
63	`p` is trivial, then `M` localizes to zero on a basic-open neighbourhood of `p` — some
64	`f ∉ p` has `M[1/f] = 0`.

66	This is the honest "the module's support avoids `p`; shrink to the support-free
67	neighbourhood" step: `M ⊗ κ(p) = 0` places `p` outside the (closed, for a finite module)
68	support `Z(Ann M)`, so a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` misses the support entirely. -/
69	theorem exists_subsingleton_away_of_residueField_tmul [Module.Finite R M]
70	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
71	    (h : Subsingleton (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R] M)) :
72	    ∃ f ∉ p.asIdeal, Subsingleton (LocalizedModule.Away f M) := by
73	  have hns : p ∉ Module.support R M := by
74	    rw [Module.mem_support_iff_nontrivial_residueField_tensorProduct,
75	      not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton]
76	    exact h
77	  haveI : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M) :=
78	    Module.notMem_support_iff.mp hns
79	  exact LocalizedModule.exists_subsingleton_away p.asIdeal

81	/-- **Relative-local BPF Nakayama neighbourhood** (`spec-dd4-seam` §2.3, residue field on
82	the right): the orientation the seed's fibre comparison produces, where the fibre is
83	written `M ⊗ κ(p)` with the pure tensor `· ⊗ₜ (1 : κ(p))`. Transported from
84	`exists_subsingleton_away_of_residueField_tmul` across `TensorProduct.comm`. -/
85	theorem exists_subsingleton_away_of_tmul_residueField [Module.Finite R M]
86	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
87	    (h : Subsingleton (M ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
88	    ∃ f ∉ p.asIdeal, Subsingleton (LocalizedModule.Away f M) :=
89	  exists_subsingleton_away_of_residueField_tmul p
